title: Measuring with non-standard units
examples: Can we measure the table with your hands?
Are cubes always the same size?
What if we use different sized blocks?

explain.say: You can measure how long something is with cubes. Cubes are small blocks.
Put the cubes in a line along the pencil. Start at one end. Push the cubes close together.

draw.text: Cubes in a line, end to end

explain.say: Count the cubes from one end to the other. The pencil is six cubes long.
You can measure with your hand span too. Stretch your thumb and little finger wide.

draw.text: Hand span: thumb to little finger

explain.say: Use cubes that are all the same size. Then every count is fair.
A grown-up has a bigger hand span. So a grown-up counts fewer hand spans.

faq.q: Why must the units be the same size?
faq.a: If your units are different sizes, your measurement will be wrong. We need everything to be equal to count correctly.
asks: Do the units have to match?
Why can't I use big and small things?

faq.q: Can I use my hands to measure everything?
faq.a: You can use handspans for some things, but cubes are better for straight lines. Different tools are good for different jobs.
asks: What is the best thing to measure with?

faq.q: How do I know how many cubes long something is?
faq.a: You line the cubes up end to end until you reach the end of the object. Then you count them all.
asks: How do I count the blocks?

faq.q: Is my handspan always the same size?
faq.a: Your hand span stays about the same today, and it grows as you grow. Other people have different hand spans. A ruler gives everyone the same answer.
asks: Is my hand always the same?
Can I use my hand for measuring?

faq.a: A non-standard unit is anything we use to measure that is not a proper ruler. Cubes and handspans are examples.
asks: Give me an example of a non-standard unit.

facts: Cubes can be used to measure the length of objects.
A hand span is the distance from the tip of your thumb to the tip of your little finger, with your hand stretched wide.
For measuring to be accurate, all units must be the same size.
We can use cubes or handspans to estimate length.

quiz.say: Count the cubes along the pencil. Tap how long it is.
quiz.why: There are five cubes along the pencil. So it is five cubes long.

wrong.0: One cube was counted twice, so touch each cube just once.
wrong.2: One cube was missed, so touch each cube as you count.

quiz.say: Count the hand spans across the book. Tap how long it is.
quiz.why: Four hand spans fit across the book. So the book is four hand spans long.

wrong.0: The book was measured with hands, so the unit is hand spans.
wrong.1: One hand was counted twice, so touch each hand just once.

quiz.say: A child and a grown-up measure a table. Who counts more spans?
quiz.why: A child has a smaller hand span. So the child needs more spans to cover the table.

wrong.0: A big hand covers more of the table, so the grown-up counts fewer spans.
wrong.2: The hands are different sizes, so the counts are different too.
